claims.title: Customer order details are readable on an unverified app-to-device channel
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:entity:customer>process:mobile-app>browse-and-order`, an attacker able to observe the customer-device path can intercept browsing activity and order details sent to `process:mobile-app`. This is conditional on the unverified transport attribute, not an assertion that the channel is plaintext. The captured order context can enable targeted phishing or later attempts against the customer-facing ordering path.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:customer>process:mobile-app>browse-and-order` has unverified transport protection and an observer needs a position on the customer-device path. Impact is medium because the flow carries `pii`-tagged browsing activity and order details.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encrypted app transport
mitigations.detail: Establish the transport posture for `flow:entity:customer>process:mobile-app>browse-and-order` and require TLS for all order and browsing traffic, with certificate validation in the mobile app.

claims.title: Customer details are exposed by plaintext mobile-app API traffic
claims.description: An attacker positioned on the boundary-crossing `flow:process:mobile-app>process:web-api>api-traffic` can intercept customer details because the flow uses HTTP and its `encryption_in_transit` control is stated absent. The attacker need not authenticate to `process:web-api`; observing the customer-device-to-internal-systems path reveals order-placement data. The captured identity and order information can be used to target customers or correlate later activity handled by `process:web-api`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the flow crosses from `boundary:customer-device` to `boundary:sokify-internal-systems` in plaintext, although the attacker still needs an on-path position. Impact is medium because the flow carries customer details and is tagged `pii`.

mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:mobile-app>process:web-api>api-traffic` to TLS 1.2+ and enforce certificate validation; consider certificate pinning where operationally appropriate.
Use opaque order references where possible so the API path does not carry unnecessary customer details.

claims.title: Catalogue-management SQL may be observable across the office boundary
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:catalogue-spreadsheet>process:web-api>sql-statements`, an observer on the marketing-office-to-internal-systems path can intercept SQL statements sent by `process:catalogue-spreadsheet` to `process:web-api`. Those statements disclose pricing and product-copy changes and may reveal the API's data-operation shape. This is conditional on the unverified transport attribute; the crossing relies in part on the inferred placement of `process:web-api`. The observed catalogue operations can inform targeted business or application attacks against the API.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the flow crosses from `boundary:marketing-office` to `boundary:sokify-internal-systems` with transport encryption unstated. Impact is low because the stated payload is SQL that changes prices and product copy, rather than customer-record contents.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate the spreadsheet-to-API channel
mitigations.detail: Establish the transport used by `flow:process:catalogue-spreadsheet>process:web-api>sql-statements` and require TLS with a distinct client identity for the spreadsheet automation.
Expose a narrowly scoped catalogue-management API so the client does not transmit database-oriented statements.

claims.title: Customer records may be observable on the API-to-database connection
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:web-api>store:user-database>customer-records`, an attacker with an internal network observation point can intercept customer names, addresses, and payment-card information between `process:web-api` and `store:user-database`. This is conditional on the flow's unverified transport protection, not a claim that it is currently plaintext. Captured financial and identity data can enable customer fraud and targeted compromise of accounts served by `process:web-api`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because encryption on this intra-zone connection is unstated and the attacker needs an internal on-path foothold. Impact is high because `store:user-database` is confidential and holds `pii` and `financial` data.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS for `flow:process:web-api>store:user-database>customer-records`, validate the database certificate, and use mutually authenticated service identities where supported.

claims.title: Order and delivery data may be exposed between the API and SIMS
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:web-api>process:sims>order-handover`, an attacker able to observe the internal path can intercept placed orders, including delivery addresses and stored order-contact numbers. This is conditional on the unverified transport attribute. The data can enable targeted fraud or social engineering against customers and provides context for the downstream dispatch process in `process:sims`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the flow is within `boundary:sokify-internal-systems`, encryption is unstated, and observation requires an internal foothold. Impact is medium because the order handover carries delivery-address and contact information and is tagged `pii`.

mitigations.summary: Protect the API-to-SIMS handover in transit
mitigations.detail: Verify the transport for `flow:process:web-api>process:sims>order-handover` and require TLS or mTLS for the order handover.

claims.title: Delivery addresses may be observable while SIMS writes the flat file
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:sims>store:delivery-address-flat-file>address-write`, an attacker with an observation point in the internal environment can intercept delivery addresses while `process:sims` writes them to `store:delivery-address-flat-file`. This is conditional on the flow's unverified transport attribute. Collected addresses can be correlated with intercepted dispatch information to identify customers and their expected deliveries.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the connection is internal and an attacker needs an on-path foothold while its transport protection is unstated. Impact is medium because the destination is a confidential store containing `pii` delivery addresses.

mitigations.summary: Verify and secure the SIMS-to-file write path
mitigations.detail: Determine whether `flow:process:sims>store:delivery-address-flat-file>address-write` traverses a transport channel and encrypt it where it does; restrict host-level capture access where the file is local.

claims.title: Dispatch notes may be observable between SIMS and the fax gateway
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:sims>process:fax-gateway>dispatch-note`, an attacker observing the internal path can intercept dispatch notes containing customer names and delivery addresses. This is conditional on the unverified transport attribute. The information can be combined with the outgoing fax process to identify a customer's delivery and contact context.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the path is within `boundary:sokify-internal-systems`, protection is unstated, and the attacker needs internal traffic visibility. Impact is medium because the dispatch note carries customer name and address information tagged `pii`.

mitigations.detail: Establish the transport used by `flow:process:sims>process:fax-gateway>dispatch-note` and require authenticated encryption for dispatch-note delivery.

claims.title: Customer confirmations may be intercepted on the unverified fax delivery path
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:fax-gateway>entity:customer>confirmation-fax`, an observer on the boundary-crossing fax path can intercept a confirmation carrying the customer's name and address. This is conditional on the flow's unverified transport attribute. The disclosed identity and delivery information can enable targeted impersonation or social engineering of the customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the fax confirmation crosses from `boundary:sokify-internal-systems` to `boundary:customer-device` with transport protection unstated. Impact is medium because it carries customer name and address data tagged `pii`.

mitigations.detail: Use an authenticated customer portal or another recipient-verifiable encrypted delivery method instead of `flow:process:fax-gateway>entity:customer>confirmation-fax` where possible.

claims.title: An unintended fax recipient can read customer confirmation details
claims.description: `flow:process:fax-gateway>entity:customer>confirmation-fax` sends a confirmation containing the customer's name and address, while destination verification is stated absent. A person who receives a confirmation at a stale, incorrect, or otherwise unintended fax destination can read that customer's details without needing access to Sokify systems. The recipient can use the disclosed identity and address to conduct targeted fraud or social engineering against the customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because destination verification is stated absent on a customer-bound flow crossing to `boundary:customer-device`. Impact is medium because every misdirected confirmation exposes the customer's name and address, which are `pii`.

mitigations.summary: Verify the recipient before sending a confirmation
mitigations.detail: Require a verified customer-controlled destination and confirmation or retry workflow before `process:fax-gateway` sends customer details.
Send an opaque order reference rather than customer name and address in any channel whose recipient cannot be strongly verified.

claims.title: A copied user-database volume may disclose customer and payment data
claims.description: `store:user-database` is confidential and holds customer names, addresses, and payment-card information, but its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If that unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker obtaining a disk, snapshot, backup, or decommissioned storage copy can read the records directly without using `process:web-api`. This is conditional on the at-rest encryption gap, not an assertion that the database is unencrypted. A single copied artifact can expose the whole customer corpus and enable payment fraud and identity-focused attacks.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because encryption at rest for `store:user-database` is unstated, while copied media can be read without live application access if protection is absent. Impact is high because the confidential store holds both `pii` and `financial` data for the customer population.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption for database media and copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the at-rest posture of `store:user-database`, then enforce managed-key encryption for the primary store, backups, snapshots, replicas, and decommissioned media.
Limit export, snapshot, backup, and key-use permissions to separate least-privileged operational roles and audit their use.

claims.title: A copied delivery-address file may disclose customer locations
claims.description: `store:delivery-address-flat-file` is a confidential store containing `pii`, and its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If the file is unencrypted at rest, an attacker who obtains its host storage, backup, or copied file can read delivery addresses without going through `process:sims`. This is conditional on the unverified at-rest control. The addresses can be combined with customer identity details exposed by adjacent order and fax flows to target customers physically or through social engineering.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because encryption at rest for `store:delivery-address-flat-file` is unstated and a copied file bypasses application access controls if encryption is absent. Impact is medium because the confidential file contains customer delivery-address `pii`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the delivery-address file and operational copies
mitigations.detail: Establish whether `store:delivery-address-flat-file` is encrypted at rest, then encrypt its volume and every backup or copied artifact with managed keys.
Delete addresses once dispatch no longer requires them and restrict filesystem, backup, and support access to the file.

claims.title: An unauthenticated or over-permitted API caller may elicit customer records
claims.description: `process:web-api` is internet-facing, keeps customer records in `store:user-database`, and both the API authentication mechanism and authentication on `flow:process:web-api>store:user-database>customer-records` are unstated. If the externally reachable API lacks effective authentication or per-record authorization, an outside attacker can send requests to `process:web-api` that elicit other customers' names, addresses, and payment-card data from `store:user-database`. This is conditional on the unresolved authentication and authorization posture; it is not an assertion that anonymous record access exists. Successful responses provide corpus-scale identity and financial data that can support fraud against customers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `process:web-api` is internet-facing and its authentication mechanism is not stated, although exploitability depends on the unresolved access-control design. Impact is high because `store:user-database` is confidential and contains `pii` and `financial` customer records.

mitigations.detail: Document and enforce strong authentication on `process:web-api` for every customer-data operation, with deny-by-default behavior.

Bind every customer-record read through `flow:process:web-api>store:user-database>customer-records` to the authenticated caller's ownership or narrowly scoped staff role, and log denied and bulk-read attempts.
